newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-PEREC'S CAMPAIGN ENDS IN TEARS ON TRAINING TRACK.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-PEREC'S CAMPAIGN ENDS IN TEARS ON TRAINING TRACK.

text.p: Marie-Jose Perec's world championship campaign ended in tears on the training track on Thursday when she pulled a leg muscle while warming up and was forced to pull out of the 200 metres semifinals.
The Olympic 200 and 400 metres champion, who originally did not want to compete in Athens because of her disappointing form this season, hurt a thigh muscle and left the warm-up arena in tears.

"She was training with (coach) John Smith and some of the other athletes and she pulled a thigh muscle," French team official Richard Descoux said. "One of the French officials Jean-Claude Volmer saw her and noticed that she was crying and he asked why."
Smith added: "She was finishing the warm-up when she suddenly felt a twinge in her leg, her right hamstring. She started to walk and then the leg got tighter and tighter.
"I said to her 'I'm gonna pull you out, there is no point in you getting hurt'. It was my decision. She was very disappointed, obviously."
French team doctor Herve De Labareyre said Perec had strained a thigh muscle.
"I went to see her straight away but all we could do was put ice on it. She was obviously disappointed. We are not sure how bad it is but she will be out for at least three weeks."

Perec entered the 200 only here and admitted that it would need a miracle for her to win a medal. But she had looked confident in the earlier heats and could have had a chance of getting into the first three in Friday's final.
Defending champion Merlene Ottey, who failed to win a medal in the 100 metres, looked sharp as she won her semifinal with metres to spare in 22.26 seconds.
"I feel relaxed and good. I am pleased with that," the 37- year-old said. "This is not a life and death situation for me."

In the men's 200, Trinidad's Ato Boldon, who finished a disppointing fifth in the 100 final, looked in impressive form, winning his heat in 20.09. Namibia's Frankie Fredericks, the 1993 champion, took second with relative ease in 20.18.
Boldon, who trains with Perec, said the Frenchwoman had had no chance of competing.
"If she had come out and run today she would have left the track on a stretcher," he said.
